name: Book confirmed appointments in Google Calendar

parameters.content:
## Book confirmed appointments in Google Calendar

### Purpose and audience
For teams connecting a booking form, assistant or internal tool to Google Calendar. Accept a request that the caller has already confirmed, check the requested interval and create a private calendar event only when that interval is available. This workflow does not obtain the person's confirmation itself.

### How it works
The webhook validates real RFC3339 timestamps, a future start, an interval of at most one day, a summary and a request ID. The request must include `confirmed: true`. Calendar availability must be an explicit boolean. After creation, the workflow checks the returned event ID, confirmed status and times before reporting success.

### Setup
1. Configure a Webhook Header Auth credential on Receive Request. Send that header from your caller and choose a unique webhook path. Never put secrets in this note or in the request body.
2. Select your Google Calendar OAuth credential on both Google Calendar nodes. Replace both `YOUR_CALENDAR_ID` placeholders with the same calendar ID.
3. Start with a dedicated test calendar. Keep the workflow inactive until your installation, credentials, caller and error paths have been tested.
4. Send `start`, `end`, `summary`, `request_id` and boolean `confirmed`. Timestamps need seconds and an explicit offset. The summary must be nonempty and at most 160 characters. The request ID must contain 16 to 64 lowercase letters a to v or digits.
5. Keep the same request ID for retries of the same intended booking. Use a different ID for a different booking.

### Responses and limits
HTTP 201 means the matching event receipt was confirmed. HTTP 400 means invalid input. HTTP 409 means the interval is busy and this attempt did not create a new event. HTTP 502 means the calendar check failed or creation remains unconfirmed. Inspect the response status to distinguish those cases.

Availability checking and event creation are separate operations. Serialize all calendar writers if overlapping reservations are unacceptable. This workflow provides no exactly-once guarantee. After an ambiguous response, reconcile the request ID in the calendar before retrying; a busy retry can reflect the earlier successful event.

Events have no attendees, confirmation emails or reminders. Separate workflows are needed for customer notifications, rescheduling and cancellation. Isolated fixture checks do not establish a successful n8n import or live provider behavior. Test valid, invalid, busy, provider-error, ambiguous and repeated requests in your own installation before activation.

Created by [Benian](https://benian.ai).

parameters.content:
### Request and validation
Require Header Auth and caller confirmation before use. Validate the timestamp, interval, summary and stable request ID. Invalid input returns HTTP 400 without reaching the calendar.

A successful validation is not a reservation. The next step must check availability before any event is created.

### Availability and concurrency
Both Google Calendar nodes must use the same calendar. Only explicit available=true continues to creation. Busy intervals return HTTP 409; errors or malformed availability return HTTP 502.

Keep all writers serialized when double booking is unacceptable. The check and creation do not form one atomic reservation.

### Receipt and retries
HTTP 201 requires a confirmed event with the requested ID and exact times. Creation errors or a mismatched receipt return HTTP 502 with an unconfirmed status.

Before retrying an ambiguous result, look up request_id in Google Calendar. Reuse that ID for the same intended booking. A later busy response does not prove the earlier attempt failed. No customer confirmation is sent.
